- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is trending down, avoid excessive downward bias; add 3–5% upward adjustment to prevent premature bottoming.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model tends to overreact; cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high to prevent overshoot.  
- Mean reversion is stronger in low-sentiment periods; if sentiment <0.3 for 3+ days, apply 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, if last 5 days show strong downward momentum, forecast should not exceed 10% above recent low; otherwise, risk overfitting to recent noise.  
- If sentiment history shows rising from 0.0–0.5, model often underreacts; add 2–4% upward bias to forecast to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
